issues.message: In main, each insertion is written as `head = push_front(head, ...)`, which discards the only live pointer to the existing chain whenever the call fails. push_front documents and implements a failure contract (malloc returning NULL yields NULL with 原链表不变), so on a reachable path — e.g. malloc fails on the call that inserts 2 — the assignment overwrites the pointer to the node holding 1 with NULL: that node (and any earlier nodes) becomes unreachable and is never released by the subsequent free_list(head), i.e. a memory leak. The comment '分配失败，原链表不变' is accurate only for the function body, not for the caller, which does lose ownership. Use a temporary, e.g. `struct Node *n = push_front(head, 2); if (n == NULL) { /* keep head, report error */ } else head = n;`, so that a failed allocation neither leaks nor silently empties the list.
